Síntesis

OntoExhibit es el resultado de transformar y ampliar el modelo conceptual subyacente a Expofinder, una base de datos relacional desarrollada en el marco del proyecto Exhibitium (Rodríguez-Ortega, Cruces-Rodríguez, 2019). El modelo Expofinder se adhiere a la concepción tradicional del campo de las exposiciones: una red formada por las relaciones que las exposiciones establecen entre actores heterogéneos (artistas, curadores, instituciones, etc.) y los objetos culturales exhibidos. Este modelo sirvió como punto de partida para el diseño y construcción del modelo OntoExhibit, que es una versión mejorada nacida de una conceptualización refinada del campo de las exposiciones. Este desarrollo se nutrió de extensas conversaciones y diálogos con una comunidad diversa de investigadores, curadores, galeristas y críticos de arte. OntoExhibit interpreta el dominio de la exposición de arte como un ecosistema cultural complejo, que comprende una amplia gama de actores (incluyendo entidades humanas y no humanas) entrelazados a través de prácticas discursivas y sociales. Estas prácticas crean una compleja red de capas semánticas que imbuyen al dominio de valores simbólicos. OntoExhibit, por tanto, aborda el fenómeno de las exposiciones de arte en su doble condición: como una producción discursiva, social y cultural diferenciada que emerge de un conjunto de prácticas e interacciones, y como productora/generadora activa de discursos y esferas públicas. Estas esferas públicas, a su vez, están configuradas por prácticas discursivas y sociales que también transmiten significados y generan valor simbólico, lo que puede influir en exposiciones posteriores. Esto crea un ciclo dinámico y continuo de impacto cultural y significado. De acuerdo con esta conceptualización, OntoExhibit tiene como objetivo profundizar nuestra comprensión de las estructuras, redes y patrones de comportamiento dentro de este ecosistema cultural; desentrañar sus complejidades sociales, discursivas y semánticas; y mejorar nuestra comprensión de la interacción de individuos y comunidades con el patrimonio cultural a través de las exposiciones. Para este fin, OntoExhibit integra los enfoques tradicionales de modelado del dominio de las exposiciones de arte con nuevas extensiones.

Introducción volver a índice

OntoExhibit se está alineando con ontologías de referencia, específicamente con CIDOC-CRM (7.2.1.) y FRBRoo (3.0). Estas ontologías han informado la definición de algunas de las clases y propiedades, mientras que se están creando nuevas clases y propiedades para responder a los requisitos del dominio de la exposición de arte tal como se define en la sección 1. Esta no es una especificación de CIDOC-CRM como tal, ya que solo se han adoptado algunas entidades y propiedades para facilitar la alineación. OntoExhibit presenta una estructura conceptual y una jerarquía de clases diferente a la de CIDOC-CRM, que se adapta mejor a la configuración actual del dominio de las exposiciones de arte y a la conceptualización de este fenómeno como un ecosistema cultural complejo (Rodríguez Ortega, en prensa). Esta investigación ha sido financiada por el Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación (Gobierno de España), número de ayuda PID2021-125037NB-I00, y por la Junta de Andalucía, números de ayuda PY20_00508, UMA20-FEDERJA-126. Ontologías de referencia - frbroo: https://www.iflastandards.info/fr/frbr/frbroo.html - cidoc-crm: http://www.cidoc-crm.org/cidoc-crm/ Patrones de diseño de ontologías de referencia - agentRole: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/cp/owl/agentrole.owl

OntoExhibit: Descripción volver a índice

OntoExhibit consiste en una ontología OWL 2 (Ontology Web Language) diseñada para facilitar la adopción de los principios FAIR (Encontrables, Accesibles, Interoperables y Reutilizables) en la gestión de la información asociada con el dominio de las exposiciones de arte, como medio fundamental para garantizar su estandarización, interoperabilidad, reutilización y la extracción de nuevo conocimiento estratégico dentro de este sector cultural. En este contexto, OntoExhibit se concibe como una ontología integral diseñada para abordar las necesidades y requisitos de una variedad de escenarios objetivo: 1. historiadores del arte e investigadores dedicados a estudios curatoriales y de exposiciones; 2. profesionales del patrimonio cultural involucrados en el registro y documentación de exposiciones de arte; 3. curadores independientes y de museos; 4. galeristas; y 5. partes interesadas en las industrias culturales y creativas (ICC) y el turismo.

Términos de OntoExhibit para clases, propiedades de objeto y propiedades de datos volver a índice

actantec Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Actant

This class comprises entities that engage in a role or perform specific activities, either on their own initiative or mobilized by other entities. In the context of the OntoExhibit ontology, it refers to those entities that play an active role in the art exhibition domain. This class is broader than the CIDOC-CRM E39 Actor class, which is limited to human entities. Additionally, the decision to use the term "actant" over the more conventional term "actor" stems from the Greimasian tradition, where the condition of being an actant is determined by the specific role or function that an entity performs. In contrast, the term "actor," as currently associated with the concept of actor in Bruno Latour's actor-network theory, is defined by its capacity to exert agency. Acknowledging that any entity might possess agency within a specific context or time, the class labeled as “actor” would be all-encompassing, including all classes. Conversely, designating a distinct class as "actor" would restrict agency value to those classes classified as subclasses of actor.
equivalente a
any U R I

actante no humanoc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Non_Human_Actant

A non-human entity that plays an active role in the realm of art exhibitions. This may include biological entities, such as animals and plants, as well as inanimate objects, that actively participate in the creation, interpretation, or presentation of artworks and cultural productions. This class is essential for addressing the participation of non-human entities that affect or contribute to artistic dynamics in significant ways. For example, an installation may include living plants, where their biological processes (such as growth, photosynthesis, and response to light stimuli) are monitored and used to alter other elements of the installation, such as lighting, sounds, or visual projections. Sensors placed on the plants detect changes in their environment (such as humidity, temperature, and light) and these data trigger modifications in the installation, creating an environment that is co-created by the biological activity of the plants. This class does not comprise technological entities which, in the context of the OntoExhibit ontology, are considered to inherently carry a human component in their design, conceptualization, and execution. See “Techno-Actant” class.
tiene superclases
actante c

actividadc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Activity

This class comprises specific, goal-oriented actions and operations carried out by a single agent or a collective. Activities are concrete, distinguishable events situated in a spatio-temporal context, typically involving coordination, resources, and participation. They may lead to material or conceptual outcomes, and include both transformative processes (e.g., creation, production, curation) and planned or programmed activities (e.g., concerts, lectures, openings).

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Scholarly_Educational_Activity

The "Academic-Educational Activity" class represents activities designed to provide educational or scholarly value to participants. These activities are aimed at enhancing knowledge, fostering learning, and promoting academic inquiry within the context of art exhibitions and cultural events. Academic-Educational Activities include workshops, lectures, seminars, guided tours, educational programs, and other instructional sessions intended for students, educators, researchers, and the general public.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Communication_Activity

The "Communication Activity" class represents any activity aimed at conveying information, promoting events, engaging with audiences, or facilitating interaction and dialogue. This includes a wide range of activities such as public relations campaigns, social media interactions, press releases, newsletters, and other forms of communication that support the dissemination and reception of information related to art exhibitions and cultural events.

actividad programadac Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Planned_Activity

The "Planned Activity" class represents any type of event that is systematically scheduled and organized ahead of time, often of significant interest, that takes place at a specific time and location. This includes a wide range of activities such as exhibitions, performances, lectures, workshops, openings, and other cultural or social gatherings. These activities are characterized by their temporality, purpose, and the involvement of participants or an audience. They are organized to achieve specific objectives, such as education, entertainment, community engagement, or celebration.

Propositional Activity designates a planned activity whose defining component includes one or more propositions articulated as its propositional content. It covers activities in which statements, arguments, interpretations, or discursive framings are central to what the activity is and does, enabling them to be related to "Proposition" via "conveys" within OntoExhibit.

afiliaciónc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Affiliation

Affiliation is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that records a formal staff relationship between an individual and an organisation. It captures cases in which a person is affiliated with an institution through employment or an equivalent contractual arrangement, performing defined roles and responsibilities within the organisation during a specific time range (and, where relevant, under particular terms or statuses). In OntoExhibit, Affiliation supports the analysis of institutional labour and professional trajectories by making staff relationships explicit, time-qualified, and queryable, without reducing them to a timeless link between a person and an organisation.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Assignment

The "Assignment" class represents the action of assigning attributes, propositions, statements, evaluations, critical assessment, interpretations, or similar elements to entities. This action involves linking specific descriptive, interpretative or evaluative contents to artworks, exhibitions, cultural creations and events, or any relevant subjects within the domain. The Assignment class is essential for providing additional context, meaning, or evaluation to entities, thereby enhancing understanding, interpretation, and scholarly analysis.

The "Interpretation Assignment" class represents the act or process of assigning a specific interpretation, meaning, or analysis to an entity or work. This class encompasses various activities involved in the contextualization, explanation, and understanding of an entity's significance, including the assignment of thematic, historical, cultural, or conceptual interpretations. Interpretation Assignments can be applied to artworks, texts, events, or any other entities that require deeper analysis and understanding.

contexto biográficoc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#biographical_context

Biographical context is a subclass of Spatio-temporal context used to model time-qualified circumstances that shape an individual’s life history and trajectory. It groups intermediary constructs that connect a person to places, situations, or other biographical conditions while accounting for change over time (e.g., moving between residences or shifting life settings). Rather than treating such relations as fixed attributes of a person, Biographical context represents them as contextual records anchored to a defined time range, enabling the reconstruction and analysis of biographical geographies and temporal sequences.
tiene superclases
contexto espacio-temporal c
tiene subclases
residencia c

contexto espacio-temporalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#spatio-temporal_context

Spatio-temporal context is a superclass for intermediary (reified) constructs that qualify relationships by explicitly attaching them to a time range and, when relevant, to a spatial setting or other contextual parameters. It is used to model situations in which a link between an actant (person, collective, institution) and an entity such as a place, an organization, a role, or a position must be expressed as historically variable rather than fixed. Instances of this class therefore function as contextual “records” that capture how a relationship holds during a specific period (and potentially in specific locations), supporting the representation of change over time (e.g., moving residence, shifting memberships, evolving professional affiliations, or relocating areas of activity). In OntoExhibit, Spatio-temporal context provides a shared modeling pattern for biographical and professional/institutional histories—such as Residency, Place of Activity, Membership, Representation, Executive Position, and Affiliation—by separating the stable entities involved (actants, places, organizations) from the time-qualified contexts that connect them. This design enables robust querying and comparative analysis of trajectories, networks, and spatial distributions across the exhibition ecosystem without conflating entities with the temporalized circumstances in which their relations are enacted.
tiene subclases
contexto biográfico c, contexto institucional c, contexto profesional c

contexto institucionalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#institutional_context

is a subclass of Spatio-temporal context that groups intermediary (reified) constructs used to describe time-qualified institutional configurations and organisational circumstances. It is intended to model historically variable institutional arrangements—such as official locations, centres, and infrastructural presences—without reducing them to timeless attributes of the organisation or to the intrinsic nature of places. In OntoExhibit, Institutional context provides a shared pattern for representing how collective actants are situated and structured across time through formal, institutionally recognised relations to physical and/or techno-digital places.
tiene superclases
contexto espacio-temporal c
tiene subclases
centro institucional c, emplazamiento c

contexto profesionalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#professional_context

Professional context is a subclass of Spatio-temporal context used to model time-qualified relations through which actants participate in professional, institutional, and organisational environments. It groups intermediary constructs that connect people or collectives to places of activity, memberships, affiliations, representative roles, or executive positions, capturing how these relations evolve across time and (when relevant) across space. By reifying these links as contextual records, Professional context supports analyses of careers, networks, institutional trajectories, and the shifting infrastructures through which cultural work is organised within exhibition ecosystems.
tiene superclases
contexto espacio-temporal c
tiene subclases
afiliación c, lugar de actividad c, membresía c, puesto ejecutivo c, representación c

dispositivoc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Dispositif

In OntoExhibit, the "Dispositif" class represents a category that encompasses entities functioning as elements for documenting exhibitions, communicating information about them, facilitating their understanding, expanding their ideas, and more. This class includes various types of dispositifs such as documentation tools, communication materials, mediation activities, interpretative aids, and expansion apparatuses. A dispositif serves to enhance engagement, comprehension, expansion, and dissemination of knowledge related to exhibitions, making it a crucial component in the art exhibition domain’s discursive and social practices. Although in OntoExhibit this class is specifically designed to codify information about exhibitions, it can also be applied to other events and objects.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Communication_Dispositif

The "Communication Dispositif" class represents materials and events used to communicate and disseminate information about cultural activities and productions. These dispositifs typically include press releases, brochures, websites, social media posts, newsletters, and other structured systems or media that convey information to the public and stakeholders. Additionally, other objects and materials can also serve this purpose. Therefore, this class links cultural activities and productions with those propositional objects and events that inform about them, regardless of their nature, genre, or typology.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Institutional_Communication_Dispositif

The "Institutional Communication Dispositif" class represents official materials and events used by institutions to communicate and disseminate information about cultural activities and productions. These dispositifs function as authoritative sources of information, providing legitimacy and formal recognition to the messages conveyed. Examples include institutional press releases, official brochures, institutional websites, social media channels managed by the institution, newsletters, and other structured communication systems.

dispositivo de comunicación no institucionalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Non-Institutional_Communication_Dispositif

The "Non-Institutional Communication Dispositif" class represents unofficial materials and events used to communicate and disseminate information about cultural activities and productions. These dispositifs often include contributions from individuals, artists, independent groups, and grassroots organizations. They may reflect personal perspectives or community-driven initiatives. Examples include personal blogs, independent social media posts, artist statements, community newsletters, zines, and other forms of informal communication. The non-institutional nature of these dispositifs underscores their role in offering diverse and decentralized forms of communication within the cultural sector.

dispositivo de documentaciónc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Documentation_Dispositif

The "Documentation Dispositif" class represents propositional objects used to document or register information, data, evidences, features, etc. with the aim of recording and preserving information about something. Classes that are susceptible to be documented are events, material objects, conceptual works, and places. Various propositional objects are typically employed for these purposes, including catalogs, records, inventories, databases, and other structured documentation systems that capture, organize, and store information. Additionally, other propositional objects can also serve this purpose, such as artworks, maps, diagrams, personal photograph albums, socially-built archives, etc., although they have not been primarily conceived or designed for this end. Therefore, this class links entities with those propositional objects that document them regardless their nature, genre, or typology.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Institutional_Documentation_Dispositif

The "Institutional Documentation Dispositif" class represents official documentation tools and mechanisms used by institutions to record, organize, and legitimize information about events, activities, and objects. These dispositifs function as authoritative sources of information, providing legitimacy and formal recognition to the documented entities. Examples include official records, registries, institutional databases, and certified archival materials. The institutional nature of these dispositifs underscores their role in establishing and maintaining authoritative narratives and histories within the institutional framework.

dispositivo de documentación no institucionalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

The "Non-Institutional Documentation Dispositif" class represents unofficial documentation tools and mechanisms used to record and interpret information about events, activities, and objects. These dispositifs often include socially constructed materials, contributions from artists, and other informal or non-official sources. They may reflect personal perspectives, creative interpretations, or community-generated content, providing alternative narratives and insights that complement or challenge institutional records. Examples include personal archives, artist's notebooks, community-led documentation projects, and other forms of grassroots or independent documentation.

These dispositifs include supplementary materials, interactive media, extended narratives, academic publications, discussion forums, and other materials and activities designed to deepen and broaden the audience's engagement and understanding of the cultural activities and productions. Additionally, other propositional objects and activities can also serve this purpose. Therefore, this class links cultural activities and productions with those propositional objects and activities that expand their understanding and interpretations, regardless of their nature, genre, or typology.

The "Institutional Expansion Dispositif" class represents official materials and activities used by institutions to expand the interpretations, readings, discourses, ideas, and understanding of cultural events and objects. These dispositifs function as authoritative mechanisms for broadening and deepening the understanding and engagement with cultural content. Examples include institutional publications, official social media campaigns, lectures, academic conferences, and collaborative projects with other cultural or educational institutions. The institutional nature of these dispositifs underscores their role in delivering institutionally legitimized means for enriching and expanding the cultural narrative and intellectual engagement.

These dispositifs are often created and distributed by individuals, artists, independent groups, or grassroots organizations. They provide alternative and diverse methods for broadening and deepening engagement with cultural content, reflecting personal perspectives, creative interpretations, or community-driven initiatives. Examples include independent publications, artist-led discussions, community workshops, blogs, zines, and other informal media. IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Location

Location is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that links a collective actant (e.g., a group, community, or corporate body) to the place(s) where it is situated during a specific time range. It is designed to represent organisational location as historically variable rather than as a fixed attribute, allowing multiple location records to coexist for the same entity across different periods. In OntoExhibit, Location is primarily used to connect collective actants to geographical territories or techno-digital places that function as their institutional points of presence (for example, a headquarters city and an official website or platform). This makes it possible to describe complementary forms of location—physical and techno-digital—without conflating them with broader activity geographies. In contrast to Place of Activity, which captures the distributed set of places where an actant operates professionally, Location captures where an organisation is formally situated in a given period; for individual actants, the analogous biographical construct is Residency.

Propositional Entities encompass a wide range of forms, including artworks, exhibitions, catalogs, literary works, scholarly works, performances, lectures, conferences, and other entities that communicate or represent specific meanings, concepts, or messages. These entities are characterized by their capacity to convey and embody propositional content, which may involve thesis, hypotheses, interpretations, critical discussions, etc.

The "Social Digital Place" class represents digital environments designed to enable social interactions, communication and social engagement among users. Social Digital Places include social media platforms, online forums, and other digital venues that enable users to connect, share, and interact in a social context. lugarc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://cidoc-crm.org/cidoc-crm/7.1.1/Place

Place represents any spatial or locative context in which events, practices, or cultural processes are situated. It covers a broad spectrum of locations, ranging from geopolitical entities (e.g., countries, regions, cities) and built environments (e.g., buildings, rooms, exhibition halls) to techno-digital environments (e.g., online platforms, virtual spaces, networked interfaces). The class is intended to support the description of the multiple spatial conditions under which art is produced, curated, mediated, displayed, and experienced. Place is broader than CIDOC CRM’s E53 Place, which is restricted to physical space. OntoExhibit maintains compatibility with CRM by allowing physical places to align with E53 where appropriate, while also accommodating techno-digital places that fall outside CRM’s strictly physical scope.

lugar de actividadc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Activity_Place

Place of Activity is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that links a human actant (or collective) to one or more places in which they carry out professional activities during a defined time range. It is intended to capture activity geographies that may be distributed across multiple locations rather than reducible to a single, fixed base. For example, an art gallery may operate through branches, fairs, collaborations, or recurring programs in several cities beyond the city where its main office is located. In OntoExhibit, Place of Activity supports the analysis of dispersed cultural work and the spatial dynamics of professional trajectories. The set of places connected to an actant through successive or concurrent instances of Place of Activity constitutes the actant’s broader area of activity, enabling comparative study of mobility, networked operations, and the territorial and techno-digital reach of actors within exhibition ecosystems.
tiene superclases
contexto profesional c

lugar de procesosc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#process_locus

Process Locus designates a place understood in its role as the spatial (territorial or techno-digital) locus of a process relevant to curation and/or exhibition making and its associated chains of cultural production. Rather than defining a place by its intrinsic nature (e.g., territory, building, platform), this class captures a contextual function: a place becomes a Process Locus when it is referenced as the location where specific processes occur—such as conception, curation, creation, foundation, dissolution, or destruction—within the broader ecology of exhibitions, artworks, institutions, and cultural agents. In OntoExhibit, Process Locus is introduced to make explicit the often distributed and multi-sited character of exhibition work. It enables the ontology to distinguish between the frontstage geography of display (e.g., venues/sites where exhibitions are presented) and the backstage geography of production and organization (e.g., where curatorial, creative, and institutional processes are carried out, which may be remote, outsourced, or platform-based). A single place (for instance, a city, a workshop, a museum building, or an online environment) may function as a Process Locus in some contexts and not in others; therefore, Process Locus should not be interpreted as a permanent subtype of place, but as a role inferred from its participation in process-location relations. By providing a shared conceptual handle over heterogeneous place types, Process Locus supports comparative analysis across cases (e.g., identifying off-site or techno-digital loci of conception and curation, mapping distributed production networks, and measuring degrees of spatial decoupling between production and exhibition). This makes it particularly useful for exhibition studies and curatorial research focused on infrastructures, labor, and the spatial politics of cultural production.

lugar c

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Membership

Membership is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that models the relationship by which an individual or collective human actant participates as a member of a group or corporate body. It represents membership as historically contingent rather than permanent, allowing the association of the member and the membership organisation with a defined time range and, where relevant, with additional qualifying terms (e.g., type of membership, status, or conditions of participation). In OntoExhibit, Membership supports the analysis of institutional and collective engagement by making membership explicit, queryable, and comparable across different organisations and periods. This class is broader than foaf:membershipClass, which constrains membership organisations to instances of foaf:Group. In OntoExhibit, the category of Collective Human Actant encompasses both groups and corporate bodies, and either may function as a membership organisation; Membership therefore provides a more flexible pattern aligned with exhibition ecosystems and their heterogeneous organisational forms.

objeto culturalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Cultural_Work_Manifestation

The "Cultural Work Manifestation" class represents cultural objects and productions that fall outside the traditional Western concept of "artistic" objects. This class encompasses a wide range of cultural works that are significant in their own right but do not fit the specific connotations and constructions associated with the Western concept of art. Examples include traditional crafts, indigenous artifacts, cultural rituals, folkloric expressions, community-based creations, and other forms of cultural manifestations. The purpose of this class is to provide a more inclusive framework for classifying and understanding cultural productions that cannot be categorized as "artworks" within the Western paradigm.
tiene superclases
manifestación de obra c

objeto de informaciónc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Information_Object

Modeling note: Informational Object is used to assert an informational reading of an entity (it is treated as an information-bearing vehicle). This typing is not exclusive: the same entity may also be typed under other classes when a different modeling commitment is intended (e.g., when it is modeled as a publishable/citable manifestation). In ambiguous cases such as catalogs and databases, use Informational Object for their informational function, and add the additional typing only when the modeling explicitly addresses publication framing (edition/release/versioning), circulation, and reception.

The "Natural Object" class represents entities that occur naturally in the environment. These objects are not created by humans or technological processes, and include a wide range of naturally occurring materials and formations such as rocks, minerals, plants, fossils, and other elements found in nature. Natural objects can be part of art exhibitions. They may be exhibited for their intrinsic beauty, scientific interest, or cultural significance. Therefore, they can also be integral components of artworks or art installations.

Material Objects are characterized by their tangible or representational form, making them accessible to perception, interaction, or representation.

organismo corporativoc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://www.iflastandards.info/fr/frbr/frbroo#F11_Corporate_Body

A "Corporate Body" refers to an organization or group of individuals that is recognized by law as a single entity, having its own legal identity separate from that of its members. This class encompasses entities such as corporations, associations, institutions, and government agencies, which can own property, enter into contracts, sue, and be sued in their own name. The corporate body operates through a structured governance system, typically including a board of directors or similar governing body, and is established for specific purposes such as business, education, or public service. The definition of a corporate body highlights its capacity to act as a unified entity in legal, financial, and operational contexts.

puesto ejecutivoc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Executive_Position

Executive Position is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that models the formal appointment through which an individual holds a leadership role within an organisation. It captures the fact that executive authority is institutionally defined and time-bound, enabling the association of a person, an organisation, and the relevant role or office with a specific time range (and, where applicable, with additional qualifiers such as mandate type, status, or scope of responsibility). In OntoExhibit, Executive Position covers cases in which an individual—such as a company CEO, the president of a professional association, or a museum director—embodies organisational authority and is accountable for strategic direction, decision-making, and institutional representation (including speaking on behalf of the organisation). By modelling these relations explicitly, the class supports the analysis of governance structures, institutional trajectories, and leadership networks within exhibition ecosystems.

reacción emocionalc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Emotional_Reaction

The "Emotional Reaction" class represents the emotional responses elicited by artworks, exhibitions, events, or cultural entities. This includes the range of emotions experienced by individuals, such as joy, sadness, anger, surprise, and awe, in response to artistic and cultural stimuli. Emotional Reactions are important for understanding the affective impact of cultural content on audiences and can provide valuable insights into audience engagement and reception.
tiene superclases
evento c

representaciónc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Representation

Representation is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that models the formal relationship in which an organisation—typically an art gallery—represents an artist or an artists’ collective. It captures the fact that representation is historically contingent and may change over time, enabling the association of the represented actant and the representing organisation with a specific time range (and, when relevant, with particular territories or market contexts). In OntoExhibit, Representation supports the analysis of professional networks and institutional mediation, covering activities such as promotion, market brokerage (e.g., sales), and the coordination of exhibition opportunities, without reducing these complex dynamics to a simple, timeless link between artist and gallery.
tiene superclases
contexto profesional c

residenciac Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Place_Of_Residence

Residency is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that links a person to a place where they reside for a given time range. It is designed to represent residential history as a sequence of time-qualified relations rather than as a fixed attribute, allowing multiple residences to be recorded for the same individual across different periods. By capturing when and where a person lived, Residency supports the analysis of biographical trajectories, mobility patterns, and the spatial distribution of life contexts over time.
tiene superclases
contexto biográfico c

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Press_Event

The "Press Event" class represents a media-focused event organized to provide information, announcements, or updates to journalists, media representatives, and other stakeholders. This includes press conferences, media briefings, and other events specifically designed to engage the press and provide them with the necessary materials and information to report on exhibitions, new acquisitions, significant developments, or special events.

sede centralc Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#headquarter_assignment

Headquarter is an intermediary (reified) spatio-temporal context that links a collective actant (e.g., a group, community, or corporate body) to its principal physical operational site for a given time range. It represents headquarters information as historically contingent, allowing organisations to be associated with different main addresses or sites across successive periods rather than treating headquarters as a permanent attribute. In OntoExhibit, Headquarter is intended for cases—especially common in cultural organisations such as galleries—where the official physical base of operations changes over time. It should be distinguished from Location, which may record multiple simultaneous forms of organisational presence (including techno-digital places), and from Activity Place, which captures the wider set of places where an actant conducts activities beyond its principal site..

sede secundariac Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#secondary_center_assignment

This class refers to a subsidiary or additional facility of an institution, distinct from its main headquarters. This center may be the place of activities related to the institution's mission, providing supplementary services, exhibitions, or resources. It usually serves as an extension of the institution, enhancing its reach and capabilities. Example: "The Villanueva building serve as the headquarters of the Museo del Prado, whereas the Casón del Buen Retiro serves as Secondary Center."

tecnoactantec Volver a índice o Índice de clases

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Techno-Actant

A technological entity or digital and/or computational object that actively participates in the artistic process or in the conceptualization, design, development, presentation, or interpretation of exhibitions. It may include software, hardware, and automated systems. The incorporation of this class allows OntoExhibit to capture and analyze the integration and impact of advanced technologies, especially AI systems in their multiple modalities, providing a framework to understand how these technological entities modify and affect the realm of artistic exhibitions and curatorial projects. Unlike the Non-Human Actant class, in the context of the OntoExhibit ontology, it is considered that technological entities and computational and/or digital objects inherently enclosed a human component in their design, conceptualization, development, and execution, and therefore cannot be considered non-human entities in a strict sense. This class is included without prejudice to the fact that further discussion about the role these entities play in the field of artistic and curatorial production and creation, and their agency value (their possibilities and their limits) must be developed in the coming years.
tiene superclases
actante c, objeto computacional c

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Theme

Themes provide a unifying idea or focus, serving as a basis for interpretation, but they are not inherently propositional or subject to verification. IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Triennial

The "Triennial" class represents a large-scale exhibition event that occurs every three years, showcasing a curated selection of artworks, often from a diverse range of artists, disciplines, and cultural backgrounds. Triennials are significant events in the art world, designed to present contemporary art, foster international cultural exchange, and engage with global artistic trends. These events typically span several months and include various programs such as exhibitions, performances, panel discussions, workshops, and educational activities.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#Spatial_Unit

Represents a specific segment or part of a larger spatial structure that serves a distinct function or holds significance within the overall environment. This class includes rooms, halls, wings, or any other designated areas within buildings, complexes, or other types of larger spaces. For example: the “Sala Noble” (spatial unit) is the spatial unit of Palacio de Villalón (Building – physical site), which is the headquarters of Museo Carmen Thyssen (Museum – cultural institution).

has Digital Analogousop Volver a índice o Índice de propiedades de objetos

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#hasDigitalAnalogous

The "hasDigitalAnalogous" property represents a relationship between an entity and its exact digital reproduction. This property is used to link entities to their precise digital counterparts, which maintain all attributes and characteristics of the original. Examples of such digital analogues include a PDF version of a book, a digital twin of a building or city, or an exact 3D reconstruction of a physical object. The "hasDigitalAnalogous" property emphasizes the fidelity and accuracy of the digital reproduction in relation to the original entity, ensuring that the digital version tends to serve as an exact representation.

has Digital Versionop Volver a índice o Índice de propiedades de objetos

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#hasDigitalVersion

The "hasDigitalVersion" property represents a relationship between an entity and its digital counterpart, where the digital version is not merely a reproduction but a variation or interpretation of the original entity. This digital version may incorporate additional elements, contextual adjustments, or creative reinterpretations that distinguish it from a straightforward digital copy. The property emphasizes the transformative nature of the digital version, which can offer new perspectives, enhanced features, or alternative forms of engagement with the original entity. The relationship between an entity and its exact digital counterpart is defined as “hasDigitalAnalogous,” while the relationship between an activity and its mere recording is defined as “hasDigitalRecording.”

has Spatial Locusop Volver a índice o Índice de propiedades de objetos

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#hasSpatialLocus

This property relates an Event to a spatial anchor—physical or digital—used to situate the event in space when such contextualization is meaningful. It is intentionally broad and optional: many events can be spatially located in principle, but the location may be unknown, irrelevant, or not recorded. Use hasSpatialLocus for lightweight contextual placement (e.g., an interaction occurring in a messaging platform, an assignment made within an institutional system, a reaction recorded via a device), without implying that the event has a formal venue or that spatial information is a primary descriptive feature. Typical use: contextual, “if needed” spatialization of any event (including non-programmed or non-operational events).
tiene subpropiedades
takes Place At op
dominio
evento c
rango
lugar c
inversa de
is Spatial Locus Of op

takes Place Atop Volver a índice o Índice de propiedades de objetos

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#takesPlaceAt

This property relates an Activity (including both Process and Planned_Activity) to its broader place of occurrence—the territorial or techno-spatial context in which the activity unfolds. It is used to record the general geographic or infrastructural setting of an activity (e.g., a city, region, country, or a digital/technical environment), independently of the specific host site. In this model, takesPlaceAt complements hasVenue: while hasVenue points to the concrete hosting site (e.g., a museum building, gallery, institutional facility, or platform-as-site), takesPlaceAt captures the wider territorial or techno-place context that situates that venue and the activity within a larger spatial frame. Typical use: Exhibition hasVenue Villanueva building (Museo del Prado) (site) Exhibition takesPlaceAt Madrid (territorial entity) Online activities may use takesPlaceAt to indicate the relevant techno-place (e.g., a platform/ecosystem) when the broader infrastructural context matters.

IRI: https://w3id.org/OntoExhibit#apelation

The "appellation" data property represents alternative names, titles, or designations assigned to an entity, other than the official name. This property is used to specify commonly recognized names, nicknames, colloquial titles, or other forms of identification that serve to distinguish and identify the entity beyond its official designation. Instances are El Greco, Museo Reina Sofía (being the official name: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía), Big Apple (New York), El Quijote, etc.

The "identifier" data property represents a unique code, number, or string assigned to an entity within various authority vocabularies.
